items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: Fletcher Henderson had people like Buster Bailey on clarinet and J.C. Higginbotham and Hilton Jefferson, Coleman Hawkins was something else.

ctx.x: Boy I’d like to see something like that.

Yeah I think it was originally made on London Records and then it was sold to Phillips Records. I don’t even think I have a copy of it, I’ll be honest with you. Coleman Hawkins. He was unbelievable. One of a kind. When he played with Fletcher Henderson’s band in the late 20s and 30s, he stood out, as they say, like a sore thumb. That’s how powerful he was. He was just — you can’t even describe him — how he

overshadowed all the other musicians in that band, and he had some great players. Fletcher Henderson had people like Buster Bailey on clarinet and J.C. Higginbotham and Hilton Jefferson, Coleman Hawkins was something else.
